subject: Post-demo: ClearScribe model-fit recommendations + JSON-schema validator plan
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@clearscribe.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: ClearScribe model-fit recommendations + JSON-schema validator plan

Hi Sam / Claire —

Thanks again for the demo today — great context on transcription variants and the downstream summarization SLAs. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can scope a short POC: 

- Primary ask we heard: reliable structured-case summaries (case_id, timestamp, topic_tags[], summary, redaction_flags) with >95% schema compliance and predictable 99th pct latency under 600ms.
- Recommended baseline models for POC (tradeoff notes included):
  - Redwood-4b-int8 (recommended): strong latency/cost balance for short transcripts, good structured-output stability with our JSON-schema validator.
  - OpenLlama-7b-q4 (cost-sensitive): slightly higher variance on hallucination for entity extraction — requires stricter prompt conditioning and extra eval steps.
  - Redwood-13b-pt (if you want higher extractive accuracy): higher cost, recommended for long transcripts where recall matters.

Benchmarks & artifacts attached: prompt set (clearscribe_promptset_v1.json), schema example (clearscribe_schema_example_v2.json), and a short benchmark summary PDF. Also added the benchmark gist to the Drive folder.

Key items for the technical POC:
1) Structured output: we will wire a schema-first validation step. Example expected schema (short):
{
  "case_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "topic_tags": ["string"],
  "summary": "string",
  "redaction_flags": {"pii_found": "boolean"}
}

We will run the Redwood schema-linter to measure raw compliance and then report post-lint accuracy.

2) Tool/function calling: we recommend using function-calls for deterministic entity extraction (e.g., call an extractor that returns a typed JSON) and fall back to free-text generation for fuzzy summaries. We'll include a small function signature in the Drive link.

3) Retries & graceful fallback: for transient errors or KV cache misses we'll use exponential backoff + model-fallback to a cheaper variant (Redwood-4b-int8 -> OpenLlama-7b-q4) to keep latency SLOs without failing the whole pipeline.

Next steps I propose:
- Week 1 (POC kickoff): infra checklist + sample dataset (you to share 5 anonymized transcripts).
- Week 2: run initial bench and schema-compliance run; deliver a short results page.
- Week 3: iterate prompts & function signatures; production readiness checklist.

Action items for ClearScribe: please drop 5 sample transcripts to the Drive folder and confirm which compliance/PII redactions you need.

I'll follow up with a short SOW stub and the HubSpot deal link (attached).

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachments: clearscribe_promptset_v1.json (prompt set, 20 examples), clearscribe_schema_example_v2.json (schema + example outputs), redwood_quick_bench_summary.pdf (3-page PDF)

Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearScribe model-fit recommendations + JSON-schema validator plan

Thanks Irene — very helpful recap. A few clarifying Qs before we share data: 

1) Can you share a short comparison table for Redwood-4b-int8 vs Redwood-13b-pt vs OpenLlama-7b-q4 on: token cost per minute, avg latency (p50/p95), and raw schema compliance on the prompt set?

2) For the function-calling approach: does Redwood host the extractor as a function (serverless) or do we call our own extractor endpoint? We prefer ClearScribe to host the extractor to keep control of PII handling. Need guidance on auth/headers.

3) Procurement: who is the Redwood contact for an initial 3-month POC contract? Also, what's the expected start-to-production timeline if the POC looks good?

Happy to drop the anonymized transcripts once we have the contract contact.

—Sam
Sam Carter
Head of Product | ClearScribe
sam.carter@clearscribe.ai
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@clearscribe.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearScribe model-fit recommendations + JSON-schema validator plan

Sam — thanks, answers inline: 

1) Comparison snapshot (high level) — attached PDF has full numbers but summary: 
   - Redwood-4b-int8: token cost ~ $0.003/min, p50 120ms, p95 480ms, schema compliance (prompt set) ~ 88% raw -> 96% after linting & post-processing.
   - OpenLlama-7b-q4: token cost ~ $0.0018/min, p50 150ms, p95 650ms, schema compliance ~ 80% raw -> 90% post-process.
   - Redwood-13b-pt: token cost ~ $0.009/min, p50 220ms, p95 900ms, schema compliance ~ 93% raw -> 97% post-process.

2) Function-calling options:
   - Option A (ClearScribe-hosted extractor): you serve an HTTPS endpoint; Redwood calls it with a signed, time-limited JWT on each request. This keeps raw transcript control with you — recommended for PII-sensitive flows.
   - Option B (Redwood-hosted extractor): Redwood runs the extractor as a private function inside your VPC (requires Private deployment). Good if you want turnkey performance and don't want to manage scaling.

We will send a short auth pattern + example headers in the Drive folder (see Drive link).

3) Procurement contact: Monica will own the POC SOW and initial contracting. Monica — can you please take point and share a 3-month SOW template?

If POC is green, typical start-to-production for this integration: 6–10 weeks (depends on dataset and redaction constraints).

I attached the SOW stub and the detailed benchmark PDF to the Drive folder.

Best,
Irene

Sam / Claire — quick technical add-on: 

On retries / validator integration:
- We'll run a streaming response to keep p50 latency low and validate the emitted JSON in near-real-time. If the schema-linter fails, we will attempt up to 2 automatic retry attempts with small prompt adjustments (explicitly cueing field types). If retries fail, route to the extractor function (your hosted endpoint) for extraction-only path.

Validator example (pseudo):
- run: response = model.generate(prompt)
- try: parsed = json.loads(response)
- if not schema.validate(parsed):
    for i in [1,2]:
       response = model.generate(adjusted_prompt_i)
       parsed = json.loads(response)
       if schema.validate(parsed): break
    else: call extractor_endpoint(post_transcript)

I'll drop the eval script and a short containerized validator in the Drive folder (file: schema-validator-docker/).

Looking forward to the 5 sample transcripts — thanks!

Jonas
Principal ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
